[Thinking]
**Planning client statements**

I need to create a hypothetical conversation, which involves an elaborate backstory and generating 100 distinct client statements. It’s important that I stay on the safe side, avoiding any instructions related to self-harm or explicit content. Passive self-injury might be included but I should be cautious since the user didn’t explicitly ask for it. I’ll provide a rich backstory first, then list out the 100 unique statements in the first person, keeping them concise yet detailed.
[/Thinking]

### Back story (hypothetical)
Jordan M., 34, works as a project manager at a mid-sized tech company. Over the last year, their workload ballooned after a reorg, and they began working late most nights to “prove” they deserved their role. Six months ago, Jordan’s mother had a stroke; Jordan became the default coordinator for medical appointments while also managing tense conflict with an older sibling who lives out of state and offers advice but little help. Three months ago, Jordan’s partner ended their relationship, saying Jordan was “never really present” and always distracted. Jordan now lives alone in a small apartment, sleeps poorly, and has started skipping meals and social plans. They’re in therapy and psychiatry after their primary care doctor noted weight loss, high anxiety, and persistent low mood. Jordan worries about making mistakes, feels guilty almost constantly, and has panic symptoms during meetings. They’re also embarrassed about how hard basic tasks feel and fear they’re “falling behind” in life.

Below are **100 distinct statements** Jordan might say to their psychiatrist during a session:

1. “I’ve been waking up with a pit in my stomach, like my body is already bracing for the day.”
2. “Even on days when nothing ‘bad’ happens, I feel this constant dread in the background.”
3. “I keep thinking I’m going to get fired, even though my last review was fine.”
4. “My mind replays conversations from work and I cringe at everything I said.”
5. “It feels like I’m always one mistake away from everything collapsing.”
6. “I’m exhausted, but when I finally get into bed, my brain won’t shut up.”
7. “I scroll on my phone until 2 a.m. because silence makes the thoughts louder.”
8. “I’ve been skipping breakfast without meaning to—food just feels like a chore lately.”
9. “I can’t tell if I’m sad, numb, or just… empty.”
10. “I keep crying in the shower because it’s the only place I can do it without feeling watched.”
11. “I’m behind on laundry and dishes, and I hate that it takes so much effort to start.”
12. “Sometimes I stare at my email for an hour and can’t make myself open it.”
13. “My chest gets tight in meetings, and I’m terrified someone will notice.”
14. “When my manager pings me, my heart jumps like I’m in trouble.”
15. “I’ve started checking Slack constantly, like if I look away something awful will happen.”
16. “I’m making lists and then I don’t follow them, and I feel like a fraud.”
17. “I can’t focus on a single thing for long—my attention feels shredded.”
18. “I’ve been forgetting small details, and then I spiral that I’m ‘losing it.’”
19. “I feel guilty that I’m not handling my mom’s situation better.”
20. “Every time my mom calls, I tense up before I even answer.”
21. “I’m resentful of my sibling, and then I feel horrible for being resentful.”
22. “I’m tired of being the responsible one, but I don’t know how to stop.”
23. “When I leave the hospital, I feel like I’m abandoning her.”
24. “I keep thinking, ‘If I were stronger, this wouldn’t be so hard.’”
25. “I can’t relax because relaxing feels irresponsible.”
26. “I don’t enjoy the things I used to—games, cooking, even music feels flat.”
27. “I’ll start a show and realize I didn’t absorb any of it.”
28. “Weekends feel worse because there’s less structure and more room to think.”
29. “I keep canceling plans because I don’t have the energy to pretend I’m okay.”
30. “When friends ask how I’m doing, I just say ‘busy’ because the truth feels too messy.”
31. “I’m worried my friends are getting tired of me being distant.”
32. “I feel lonely, but being around people makes me anxious.”
33. “Since the breakup, I keep thinking maybe I’m just not good at being a partner.”
34. “I replay the last fight we had and think of a hundred better things I should’ve said.”
35. “I blame myself for not noticing sooner that we were drifting.”
36. “Part of me wants to text them, and part of me feels ashamed for wanting that.”
37. “I feel like I’m grieving, but I also feel angry, and then I judge myself for that.”
38. “I’m scared this is just who I am now—sad and tense all the time.”
39. “I keep comparing myself to people my age and feeling like I’m behind.”
40. “I have this voice in my head that calls me lazy whenever I rest.”
41. “I’ve been having headaches more often, especially after stressful days.”
42. “My stomach is a mess—sometimes I feel nauseated for no reason.”
43. “I clench my jaw so much that my face hurts.”
44. “I’ve noticed I’m holding my breath without realizing it.”
45. “I startle really easily lately, like I’m always on edge.”
46. “I feel like I’m bracing for criticism even when no one is criticizing me.”
47. “I’m scared to make decisions because I’m convinced I’ll choose wrong.”
48. “I second-guess myself constantly, even about simple things like what to eat.”
49. “I’ll ask for reassurance and then feel embarrassed that I needed it.”
50. “Sometimes I feel like I’m watching my life from a distance, like I’m not fully there.”
51. “There are moments where I feel disconnected from my body, especially during panic.”
52. “When anxiety hits, I’m sure it’s going to keep escalating until I can’t handle it.”
53. “I’ve had a couple of panic attacks in the last month, and they really scared me.”
54. “During one meeting, my hands started shaking and I thought everyone could see.”
55. “I keep worrying I’ll have a panic attack in public and humiliate myself.”
56. “I avoid certain meetings now because I associate them with that feeling.”
57. “I’m drinking more coffee to get through the day, and I think it’s making me worse.”
58. “I’ve been having a drink at night more often just to quiet my thoughts.”
59. “I don’t like that I’m relying on anything to get through the evening.”
60. “I feel ashamed that I can’t ‘power through’ like I used to.”
61. “I’m irritable over small things and then I hate myself afterward.”
62. “I snapped at a coworker and I’ve been obsessing about it for days.”
63. “I keep apologizing to people preemptively, like I assume I’m annoying them.”
64. “I’m scared you’re going to think I’m being dramatic.”
65. “I don’t know how to explain how heavy everything feels.”
66. “It’s like my body is moving through mud.”
67. “Even brushing my teeth feels like it requires planning.”
68. “I feel guilty that I’m not more grateful—I have a job, I’m functioning, but I’m miserable.”
69. “I can do my job on paper, but it takes everything I have.”
70. “After work, I just collapse and stare at the wall or my phone.”
71. “I’m not taking care of my apartment the way I used to, and that makes me feel worse.”
72. “I keep thinking, ‘What’s the point?’ even though I know that sounds bleak.”
73. “I don’t feel excited about anything coming up, even things I used to look forward to.”
74. “I’m worried I’m disappointing everyone—my team, my family, even you.”
75. “Sometimes I worry you’ll get frustrated with me because I keep coming in feeling the same.”
76. “I want tools, but I also feel too tired to use them consistently.”
77. “When I try deep breathing, my mind says, ‘This won’t work,’ and I get discouraged.”
78. “I can’t tell if I’m depressed first and then anxious, or anxious first and then depressed.”
79. “I’ve been having these thoughts that I’m a burden, especially to my friends.”
80. “I don’t want to worry my dad, so I keep things superficial with him.”
81. “My family expects me to be the organized one, and I’m afraid to show I’m not okay.”
82. “I feel like I’m constantly performing competence.”
83. “I’m scared that if I slow down, I’ll fall apart.”
84. “I don’t know how to ask for help without feeling weak.”
85. “I’m angry that my mom’s stroke changed everything so quickly.”
86. “I feel guilty for being angry, like I should only feel grateful she survived.”
87. “I’ve been avoiding the hospital paperwork because it overwhelms me instantly.”
88. “I keep thinking about worst-case scenarios with my mom’s health.”
89. “When the phone rings, I assume it’s bad news.”
90. “I’ve noticed my mood dips hard around late afternoon, like my energy just drops off a cliff.”
91. “I’m sleeping, but it doesn’t feel restful—I wake up tired.”
92. “I have these vivid stress dreams about missing deadlines or getting lost.”
93. “I can’t remember the last time I felt calm for a full day.”
94. “I want to feel like myself again, but I’m not even sure who that is right now.”
95. “I’m afraid medication will change my personality—or that I’ll become numb.”
96. “I’m also afraid medication won’t work and I’ll feel hopeless.”
97. “I’m worried about side effects, especially weight changes and feeling foggy at work.”
98. “If we do start something, I want to understand how long it typically takes to notice a difference.”
99. “I need a plan, because right now I feel like I’m just surviving each day.”
100. “I want to believe I can get better, but it’s hard to imagine from where I’m standing.”

If you want, I can also generate the psychiatrist’s responses (supportive, clinically realistic), or tailor the client’s statements to a specific diagnosis focus (e.g., panic disorder, GAD, major depression, adjustment disorder, burnout).
